title: Leans AI Review 2026: Pricing, Record, Is It Worth It?
description: Leans AI review, checked 7 Nov 2026: Remi pick prices from $49 a month to $27,500 a year, the no refund policy, what its scorecard leaves out, user reports.
dek: An AI pick service whose model, Remi, covers six US sports. Plans run from $49 a month to $27,500 a year, every sale is final, and the record on its site is a scorecard the seller computes itself at a flat -110 price, after retiring more than 1,058 games of older data.

status.label: Not verified
status.note: Watchdog has not graded a full, time stamped record of Leans AI picks. This page reports what we could check and labels everything else.

glance: Leans AI LLC, a Colorado limited liability company (terms page). No street address found
$49 a month (Intel) to $27,500 a year (Vault V5)

Not found. A seller computed scorecard and an undated recent picks sample
short_answer: Leans AI is a real business. Its terms name Leans AI LLC of Colorado, it publishes its prices and its rules, and it sends picks to paying members. In that narrow sense it is legitimate.

Whether Remi wins over time is not settled by anything we could open. The site shows a lifetime scorecard, for example 2,437-2,092 and +532.1 units on its Executive picks, but Leans AI computes it itself, grades every win at a flat -110 rather than the price you would get, and in August 2025 retired its older v1 and pre release data, which it says covered more than 1,058 games. We found no full log of every pick with its date, time and odds.

Treat Leans AI as a seller with an in house scorecard, not a proven winner. Its prices are high next to its own claimed edge, and no money comes back if the picks lose. If you buy, buy the shortest term, record every pick yourself with the time and the price you actually got, and judge it after a few hundred picks.
pricing_intro: Prices below were shown on the Leans AI upgrade page on 7 Nov 2026. Each level includes everything in the levels below it. The page did not state a free trial length.
pricing: Intel (pick of the day, parlay builder, underdog sleepers, marquee spotlight)
No refund. Cancel to stop renewal
Executive (2 to 5 unit game and prop picks, about 10 to 25 a week)
Vault V2 "Blackcell" (6+ unit picks, about 2 to 10 a week)
Vault V3 "Darklink" (about 4 to 20 Vault picks a week)
Vault V4 "Nightfall" (about 6 to 30 Vault picks a week)

No refund. Terms confirmed directly with qualified members
guarantee: There is no guarantee. The cancellation and refund page says Leans AI "cannot offer a refund for any fees paid with no exceptions," and lists poor results and forgetting to cancel among the cases it will not refund. The checkout box a buyer ticks says canceling stops auto renewal and that past payments are not refundable.

Subscriptions renew automatically. You can cancel in your account, and the page says you must see "CANCELS ON END DATE" or the cancellation did not work. Email cancellations must arrive at least 24 hours before renewal, and by 10 AM Eastern on the prior business day if renewal falls on a weekend or holiday. The terms also call cancellation your "sole recourse" if you are unhappy, bar chargebacks except for fraud, and let Leans AI end any account at any time without refund.

claims.claim: "AI Sports Picks Proven Across Thousands of Games"; lifetime record 2,670-2,312 against the spread, +563.4 net units after vig
Executive 2 to 5 unit picks: 2437-2092, 53.7%, 532.1 net units, "$53,212" at $100 a unit

claims_note: The numbers do not tie together on the pages we read. The homepage banner says 2,670-2,312, which matches neither the Executive table (2,437-2,092) nor the Vault table (573-467). The +563.4 units beside it is the Vault figure, and the Vault table says its units count 2 to 10 unit picks, including Executive picks, while its win and loss record counts only 6 to 10 unit picks. On the unit band table, the 9 unit row shows 50.1% over 20 picks, a rate 20 picks cannot produce, and the 2+ and 3+ rows both show 4,982 picks.

Every win is graded at a flat -110, by the FAQ's own description, and the line used is "the best line available" when the pick is released. A buyer who gets a worse number later will not match the scorecard. The FAQ also says older v1 and pre release data, "over 1,058 games worth," was retired in August 2025 and the scorecard now reflects only v2 and v3 picks, so the record you see is not the whole history since tracking began in September 2022.
record: Independently verifiable: nothing we found. We found no time stamped log of every pick held by a third party, no contest run by someone else, and no regulator or court record about results.

Seller's own marketing: a live scorecard by sport and unit size, computed by Leans AI at a flat -110 and limited to v2 and v3 picks, plus a "Recent AI Picks" list of about the last 20 picks per sport. That list shows the pick, Remi's win probability, units and result, but no date, post time or odds, and the FAQ says it is a sample that leaves out the Intel parlay, underdog and marquee picks.

The scorecard is not useless. It is detailed, it shows a losing sport (NHL is negative on both tables) and the FAQ explains its method. But a bettor cannot rebuild it from the picks, so it is a claim, not a verified record.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Leans AI pick feed is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Remi's picks perform.
our_data.context: For scale: Leans AI's own Executive scorecard shows 53.7% winners, and its founder told Vice the product is "just barely above" break even. On the Watchdog board on 7 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Leans AI is small and split. Trustpilot has the largest sample we could read, 43 reviews, and it is mixed. The testimonials on the Leans AI site are chosen by Leans AI. Below is what we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: The Leans AI homepage shows five star Trustpilot reviews from 2023 to 2025 praising transparency, unit sizing and support. They are picked by the seller, and the overall Trustpilot score is lower than the homepage suggests.

Trustpilot showed a TrustScore of 3.0 from 43 reviews: 72% five star and 14% one star. Trustpilot noted the company had not recently invited reviews, so the sample may not be representative. Only 5 reviews came in during the last 12 months.

Two one star Trustpilot reviewers said the published results did not match their experience. One, who said he had paid for Executive and Intel for several months, wrote that the models lose money. The other said losing free picks were left out of the record and asked for a complete, time stamped record. We did not verify either claim.

A Trustpilot reviewer said daily marketing emails kept coming after several unsubscribe attempts and support did not answer. The company replied that a third party email provider had been dropping unsubscribe requests.

Positive Trustpilot reviewers included one who said Remi was the only profitable system among several he had run over about eight months, while calling it streaky, and one who reported good college football results early in the 2026 season.

Price is a common complaint. A one star reviewer in 2024 said the results did not justify the cost, and a three star reviewer liked the email alerts but found the price steep and said he received only MLB picks.

A Vice writer tested Leans AI for a week, when it cost $299 a month, and called the results of his US picks patchy and mixed. The founder, who Vice said goes by the alias Steve Westfield, called it "kind of a boring product" just above the 52.4% break even rate. One week is not a sample.

RealReviews.io lists 12 reviews, mostly positive. One 2026 reviewer liked the confidence grades but called the Executive price steep. Several reviewer names and texts resemble Trustpilot reviews, so we give this site little weight.

We found no Reddit thread, no TheRX, Covers or SBR forum thread, no app store listing and no Better Business Bureau profile we could confirm belongs to Leans AI. We found no court or regulator record about the company.

conflicts: Leans AI runs an affiliate program that pays "a 30% commission on all customer purchases for their lifetime." Web pages that rank or praise AI pick tools may earn a share of what their readers pay. Weigh glowing third party write ups with that in mind.

Its terms say Leans AI does not accept or place wagers, is not associated with any sportsbook, and receives no consideration from any party with an interest in its picks. We saw no sportsbook signup or promo links on the pages we opened; its NFL odds comparison table names books such as FanDuel and DraftKings without linking to them.
strengths: A named company, published prices for every directly purchasable tier, and written cancellation steps.
The scorecard is detailed by sport and unit size, includes a losing sport, and the FAQ explains that results include vig and that past results do not predict future ones.
A free pick each day with a free account lets a reader see the format, the win probability and the unit rating before paying.
concerns: No full public record. The scorecard is computed by the seller at a flat -110, and older data covering more than 1,058 games was retired in August 2025.
The headline numbers do not reconcile across the homepage and scorecard tables.
No refunds of any kind, automatic renewal, and terms that bar most chargebacks.

High prices next to a claimed edge of a point or two: Executive costs $3,800 a year against a seller estimated $8,012 a year at $100 a unit, before any price slippage. At smaller stakes the fee can exceed the claimed profit.
Trustpilot shows 3.0 from 43 reviews while the homepage advertises five star reviews.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: It is a real business run by Leans AI LLC of Colorado, with published prices, written terms and picks delivered to members. We could not verify that Remi wins over time, because the only record is a scorecard the company computes itself.
How much does Leans AI cost?

On 7 Nov 2026 Intel cost $49 a month or $499 a year, Executive $349 a month or $3,800 a year, and the Vault tiers $5,900 to $27,500 a year, or $4,300 to $17,900 for a five month season pass. All sales are final and plans renew until you cancel.
Does Leans AI have a verified record?

No. Its scorecard is public and detailed, but Leans AI computes it at a flat -110, it covers only v2 and v3 picks after older data was retired in 2025, and we found no full time stamped log or third party audit.

You get daily model picks with win probabilities and unit ratings, a free daily pick and a detailed scorecard. What is unproven is the edge itself: the seller's own figures put it a point or two above break even, the fee is high next to that, and no money comes back if the picks lose.
